 Philippine basketball star PJ Simon dies at 46 after collapsing in Davao game
 By Nicole Anne Bugauisan
 November 21, 2026
 1230
 Resize 
 Small 
 Medium 
 Large 
 MANILA, Philippines — One of Philippine basketball's greats, Peter June “PJ” Simon, reportedly died Friday evening at 46.
 Simon collapsed while playing in a basketball league in Davao, and reports showed that he had difficulty breathing before he clutched his chest.
 The medical team made efforts to save Simon and revive him, but his pulse stopped.
 The Cotabato pride gained the moniker “Scoring Apostle,” as his efforts playing at the University of Mindanao did not go unnoticed when he collected three Most Valuable Player awards that led to him being signed by the Mindanao Basketball Association (MBA) team, Davao Eagles.
 From there, he put up a 41-point explosion in the local league, then suited up for the nation in the William Jones Cup.

 Simon took the hard route in reaching the Philippine Basketball Association (PBA) as he also had a stint with the Philippine Basketball League (PBL) in 2002, and made his stay count as he gained a 2003–04 PBL MVP award.
 This led him to his dream of stepping into the biggest basketball league in the country.
 Advertisement 
 Simon was signed as a rookie free agent by Purefoods in 2004 and worked his way to being included behind star James Yap.
 One of his highlights of his PBA career was posting a 42-point explosion on Nov. 10, 2010.
